Subject: Evaluating hardware signing appliance for BYOK + local KMS proxy

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We did an internal infra pass and have two immediate asks before we proceed to procurement: a) how the appliance will be used in our BYOK flow (operator separation, offline key import), and b) a recommended network deployment pattern for the KMS proxy inside our VPC (firewall rules, NAT, and cross-VPC peering constraints).

I've attached the vendor spec we received and our VPC diagram with basic annotations. Can your team confirm compatibility and highlight any hard blockers for an air-gapped or limited-egress deployment?

Attachments: signing-appliance-specs.pdf (PDF), vpc-network-dwg-annotated.png (PNG)

Appreciate a short response we can share with procurement.

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Feb 2025 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Evaluating hardware signing appliance for BYOK + local KMS proxy

Hi Alice — thanks for the materials. Quick summary up-front: we can support the signing appliance in a BYOK flow via our KMS proxy with two validated patterns: 1) on-prem HSM behind the customer's firewall with a local KMS proxy that holds transient wrapping keys, and 2) a 'sealed operator' model where keys are imported via an operator workstation and stored only inside the appliance (no persistent plaintext on the KMS proxy). Both patterns have trade-offs for recovery and rotation; see details below.

High-level checklist of blockers:
- Network: appliance must be reachable from the KMS proxy host on TCP/443 or the vendor port they list (see spec). For limited-e﻿gress we recommend a private peering or single-direction TLS tunnel from KMS proxy -> appliance management endpoint.
- Operator separation: recommend air-gapped import process using a USB key+signed manifest; we can document the step-by-step.
- Rotation: automated rotation can be handled by Redwood if the appliance exposes an API; otherwise we recommend a scheduled operator-assisted rotation with HSM-backed signing of rotation manifests.

We'll do a short runbook and a small architecture sketch for the two deployment modes. Marissa/Hannah — can you take the vendor spec and VPC diagram and produce: 1) an annotated network sketch (minimal flows), and 2) a short runbook for key import/rotation? Target EOD tomorrow.

Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Evaluating hardware signing appliance for BYOK + local KMS proxy

Hi All — attached is the initial annotated network sketch and the KMS proxy checklist. Key points called out:

- Minimal network flows: KMS proxy (in private subnet) -> Appliance management interface (in a management Vlan / peered subnet) on TCP/8443 (vendor port), SSH only from operator bastion (no internet).
- Egress: we do NOT require outbound internet from the appliance for signing ops; we recommend blocking outbound except for vendor update endpoints, which go through a controlled NAT with allowlist.
- NAT hole: if your compliance team restricts peering, we recommend a 1:1 NAT gateway in the management subnet to initialize vendor tunnels.
- Rotation model: we propose two rotation modes — autonomous (if appliance API supports key wrapping) or manual operator rotation with signed manifests. See rows 8–12 in checklist.

Attachments: vpc-network-dwg-annotated.png, kms-proxy-connection-checklist.xlsx

Next steps: Hannah will draft the operator import runbook and Soojin will review the RBAC/audit implications for the operator bastion. We can do a 30-min technical review with your security team tomorrow.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Alice Kerr <alice.kerr@acme-payments.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Feb 2025 10:52:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: operator import runbook draft

Alice/Team — draft runbook below (abbreviated):

1) Prepare operator workstation (air-gapped): verify signed firmware checksum, ensure workstations have ephemeral USB keys.
2) Generate CSR on appliance under operator supervision and transfer CSR via signed USB to offline signing CA if required.
3) Import wrapped key blob using vendor tool; appliance stores key in secure module, returns attestation token.
4) Redwood KMS proxy validates attestation token and persists only key reference (no plaintext).
5) Rotation: operator schedules rotation window, vendor produces new wrapped blob, operator repeats import.

Audit notes: record operator identity in attestation token and push logs to your SIEM via an encrypted syslog collector in the management subnet.

Questions: Do you need a template attestation token spec (JSON schema) for procurement?

Hannah Schmitt
Infrastructure Security | Redwood Inference
